summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on node1, remained available during a real system-wide OOM event, and recovered automatically after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Installed inventory-api listening on port 8080 with /health and /inventory endpoints.
Configured systemd restart behavior, OOMScoreAdjust=-900, and MemoryLow=64 MiB.
Ran a controlled memory hog with oom_score_adj=1000.
Verified 296/296 health checks succeeded during memory exhaustion with zero API restarts.
Confirmed the kernel OOM killer stopped memory-hog at approximately 1.69 GiB RSS.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and inventory-api recovered.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed service
evidence.summary: The systemd unit is enabled and active, uses Restart=always, listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, and serves valid health and inventory responses.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api remains available during system OOM
evidence.summary: The API stayed healthy as available memory fell to 47 MiB. The independent monitor recorded 296 successful probes, the API retained PID 1323, and NRestarts remained zero.

evidence.requirement: The kernel stops the memory hog
evidence.summary: The hog ran with oom_score_adj=1000. Kernel logs identify memory-hog PID 1517 as the OOM victim at 1,776,288 KiB anonymous RSS; systemd reports Result=oom-kill.

Pre-restart boot ID was 18d6ac04-b8ce-4113-936c-32451b2a609e; the native systemd reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to d503723c-8042-4005-ba41-199aa4aebdbb. The system returned to running state and inventory-api recovered enabled, active, protected, listening, and serving both endpoints.
